transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I've decided to come in because I've been feeling persistently depressed, sad, and down for a very long time now. It has been going on continuously for about two years and two months. I just can't seem to shake this constant low mood.

Can you tell me if there have been any periods over the past two years and two months where your depressive symptoms significantly improved for at least two months, or have they been consistently present the entire time?

I'm not quite sure if there was ever a clear two-month break where things felt better. It just feels like these heavy feelings have been consistently draining me for the entire two years and two months.
Have you experienced any significant fluctuations in the severity of your depressive symptoms over time, or have they remained relatively stable throughout the two years and two months?

They've been pretty stable and haven't really fluctuated or changed. My low mood, sadness, and lack of energy have just felt like a continuous, heavy cloud that hasn't really lifted over the entire two years and two months.
How have these persistent feelings of depression affected your daily life, such as your relationships, work, or ability to take care of yourself?

My daily life has been heavily impacted because I constantly feel physically and mentally exhausted, making even minor daily tasks feel overwhelming. I have a really hard time getting through daily activities due to this lack of energy, and I've lost confidence in my ability to handle my work or solve problems effectively.

Can you describe any periods of at least two weeks where you experienced a depressed mood or loss of interest in activities, and during those periods, did you have any symptoms such as changes in appetite, sleep, or psychomotor activity?

I have definitely felt that depressed mood continuously for over two years now. However, I haven't really noticed or thought about any specific changes in my appetite, sleep, or physical movement during this time.

Looking back over the two years and two months, can you recall if you've experienced any noticeable changes in your appetite or sleep patterns that might have coincided with your periods of low mood, even if they seem minor to you?
No, I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or sleep patterns over this period. They have stayed pretty much the same throughout these past two years.

Can you think of any times when you might have had a period of at least two weeks with either depressed mood most of the day, markedly diminished interest or pleasure in activities, or both, and at least five other symptoms like significant weight loss or gain, insomnia or hypersomnia, psychomotor agitation or retardation, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, diminished ability to think or concentrate, or recurrent thoughts of death?

I definitely experience the constant low mood, heavy fatigue, and feelings of worthlessness almost all the time. However, I haven't had a specific two-week period where these symptoms suddenly intensified or where

Did you experience at least five of the depressive symptoms, including either depressed mood or loss of interest, nearly every day for at least two weeks at any point during the past two years and two months, or have your symptoms been more chronic and less episodic in nature?

My symptoms have definitely been more chronic and persistent rather than coming in short, intense episodes. It has just been a continuous, long-term struggle with low mood, sadness, fatigue, and low self-esteem almost every single day for the entire two years and two months.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms have been consistently present for over two years with no significant fluctuations or periods of improvement, which aligns more closely with Persistent Depressive Disorder. The patient's description of a continuous, long-term struggle with low mood, sadness, fatigue, and low self-esteem without any clear episodes of intensified symptoms or significant changes in appetite, sleep, or psychomotor activity further supports this diagnosis. Major Depressive Disorder typically involves one or more major depressive episodes, which may not be the case here given the patient's chronic and persistent symptoms without clear episodic intensification.
